summary: Repaired the defect the predecessor F-5 deployment-preparation retry discovered. hpac_protected_admin_writer.py's §33 STEP 3 and hpac_foundation.py's _validate_production_boundary/_relative_record_path were independently confirmed already correctly threading the CONFIGURED PCAE agent principal's resolved (uid, gids) (from hpac_pawa_agent_exclusion.resolve_configured_agent_identity(), never os.geteuid()) through _effective_write_access/_ancestor_chain_safe -- no change required there. The actual defect lived one layer deeper: the ACL branch of _effective_write_access (_acl_grants_agent_write_linux/_acl_grants_agent_write_macos) resolved its own ACL-inspection tool (getfacl/ls) via _resolve_trusted_executable, which derives its subject from the AMBIENT _current_agent_identity() (the live invoking process) instead of the (agent_uid, agent_gids) subject already passed to it. When the canonical root-owned registration path runs, root-owned owner-writable system directories such as /usr/bin misclassify as agent[=root]-writable under that ambient question, causing acl_inspection_unavailable for every Protected-Root ancestor -- exactly the predecessor's protected_root_untrusted failure. Repair: a new sibling primitive, _resolve_trusted_executable_for_subject(name, agent_uid, agent_gids), with no ambient fallback, now serves _acl_grants_agent_write_linux/_macos. _resolve_trusted_executable itself is left completely untouched -- independently frozen by two earlier phases' own guard tests (149O.20J.1 source-content assertion, 149O.20J.2 git-diff-pickaxe def-line-unchanged guard), both reconfirmed green. Three pre-existing tests needed disclosed, non-weakening reconciliation (mocked _effective_write_access deterministically instead of relying on this host's real ACL/PATH quirk that the repair corrected). Production diff bounded to exactly src/pcae/core/hatp_class_b_topology_verifier.py. No F-5 retry, no protected-root mutation, no contract/dependency change. F-5 remains OPEN / BLOCKED PENDING REPAIR IV. N-16-5 remains NOT CLOSED.
derived_correctness: Defect traced to exact code: hatp_class_b_topology_verifier.py's _acl_grants_agent_write_linux (previously line 189) and _acl_grants_agent_write_macos (previously line 350) called _resolve_trusted_executable('getfacl'/'ls') with no subject argument, so that call fell through to _resolve_trusted_executable's own internal _current_agent_identity() (ambient euid/gids) rather than reusing the (agent_uid, agent_gids) parameters _acl_grants_agent_write_linux/_macos themselves already received from their caller. Independently reproduced deterministically: _resolve_trusted_executable('ls') resolves the real system ls under a simulated non-owning ambient subject (uid 999999) but fails closed (None) under a simulated root-like ambient subject (uid 0), because /usr/bin is root-owned and owner-writable on this host -- the exact acl_inspection_unavailable symptom. The repaired _acl_grants_agent_write_macos/_linux resolve deterministically against their real explicit subject regardless of a poisoned ambient identity.
